title: Antibiotic Mixture Exposure in Meconium Affects Child Neurodevelopment via Altering Early-Life Gut Microbiome and Metabolome.
abstract: Previous evidence has established associations of antibiotic exposure in early life with neurodevelopmental disorders. However, previous studies have often relied on self-reported or record-based exposure measures that may not accurately reflect internal fetal exposure, and few have integrated prenatal exposure biomarkers with infant microbiome, metabolome, and longitudinal neurodevelopmental data. This study included 300 mother-infant pairs from the Shanghai Maternal-Child Pairs Cohort. Meconium samples were used to quantify concentrations of 18 antibiotics using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). Neurodevelopmental outcomes were assessed using Ages and Stages Questionnaires (ASQ) at 2, 6, 12, and 24 months of age. Multi-omics profiling of 6-month fecal samples was conducted, employing 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and HPLC-based metabolomics. Linear and logistic regression models, negative binomial regression, interpretable machine learning algorithms, metabolome-wide association/pathway analyses and high-dimensional mediation modeling were used. Our study population demonstrated predominant exposure to three antibiotics: chlortetracycline, penicillin, and chloramphenicol. Each interquartile range (IQR) increase in meconium-measured antibiotic burden was associated with a lower total ASQ score at 6 months (β = -4.49, 95% CI: -7.14 to -1.86) and lower scores across all five developmental domains (βs ranging from -0.53 to -1.11; all P < 0.05). Each IQR increment of antibiotic burden was also associated with greater odds of belonging to the lower-score group of total ASQ trajectory (OR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.04, 1.42) and the lower-score group of personal-social trajectory (OR = 1.13, 95% CI: 1.01, 1.28). Exploratory high-dimensional mediation analyses identified Lactobacillus and 2-(14,15-epoxyeicosatrienoyl) glycerol (2-14,15-EG) as candidate intermediates in the association between meconium-measured antibiotic burden and neurodevelopment. Our study suggested that higher meconium-based biomarkers of intrauterine antibiotic burden were significantly associated with lower neurodevelopmental outcomes in early childhood, with the strongest inverse associations observed at 6 months. Lactobacillus and 2-14,15-EG were identified as potential mediator biomarkers. These hypothesis-generating findings require independent replication, longitudinal temporal validation, and experimental studies before causal mechanisms or microbiota-targeted interventions can be inferred.
authors: Zhou Y, Wang F, Zhao Y, Wang H, Ma W, Shi H, Zhang Y.
screening_reason: The study investigates how intrauterine antibiotic exposure affects child neurodevelopment through changes in early-life gut microbiome composition and microbial metabolomics.
summary_ja: 母子コホート300組を対象に、胎便中の18種類の抗菌薬濃度測定と生後6か月時の腸内細菌叢・代謝物メタボローム解析を行い、24か月までの神経発達との関連を調べた。胎便中の抗菌薬暴露量が多いほど、生後6か月時点のASQスコア低下および低い発達トラジェクトリーに属するリスクの上昇が観察された。高次元媒介解析により、Lactobacillus属と代謝物2-14,15-EGが抗菌薬暴露と神経発達低下を結ぶ潜在的な仲介因子として特定された。胎児期の抗菌薬暴露が乳幼児の神経発達に悪影響を与える可能性が示唆された。
summary_en: In a prospective cohort of 300 mother-infant pairs, meconium antibiotic levels were quantified alongside infant gut microbiome and metabolome profiles at 6 months to assess child neurodevelopment through 24 months. Higher internal fetal antibiotic exposure correlated with lower neurodevelopmental scores and persistently poorer developmental trajectories. Mediation analyses indicated that infant Lactobacillus levels and the metabolite 2-14,15-EG candidate-mediated these neurodevelopmental impacts.
key_finding_ja: 胎児期の抗菌薬暴露負荷は乳幼児の神経発達低下と関連し、乳児期の腸内細菌Lactobacillusと代謝物2-14,15-EGがその媒介候補として同定された。
why_it_matters_ja: 周産期抗菌薬使用のリスク評価や腸内細菌叢を介した予防介入法の開発に役立つ可能性があるが、因果関係の解明にはさらなる実証研究が必要である。

title: Antisense transcription reveals disease-associated adaptations in the human gut microbiome.
abstract: The gut microbiome is a dynamic ecosystem in which microorganisms constantly adjust their transcriptional programmes. Here we developed metastrand, a framework that integrates strand-aware metatranscriptomics and metagenomics to quantify mRNAs and antisense RNAs (asRNAs) in complex microbial communities at gene-level resolution. In inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), microbial asRNA programmes converged across patients during active disease, correlated with faecal metabolites and calprotectin levels and remained stable during persistent inflammation, highlighting their potential as biomarkers of inflammatory activity in the gut. These programmes involved antisense-to-sense transcriptional shifts at insertion sequence elements with functionally diverse passenger genes and preceded their detection at new genomic locations, linking asRNA dynamics to structural genome rearrangements and redistribution of adaptive functions under selective pressure. Similar dynamics were observed in a mouse model of colitis, oxidative stress in vitro and in patients with pathogen-confirmed gastroenteritis, establishing asRNAs as an important dimension of microbial adaptation in health and disease.
authors: Pust MM, Mohamed AMT, Stražar M, Arias-Rojas A, Cunningham-Oakes E, Brown EM, Bumber A, Pishchany G, Li C, Ananthakrishnan AN, Darby AC, Vlamakis H, Plichta DR, Xavier RJ.
screening_reason: The paper focuses on metatranscriptomic profiling of antisense RNA dynamics and transcriptional adaptation within the human gut microbiome.
summary_ja: 本研究では、ストランド認識型メタトランスクリプトミクスとメタゲノミクスを統合し、腸内細菌叢のアンチセンスRNA（asRNA）を高解像度で定量する解析ツール「metastrand」を開発した。炎症性腸疾患（IBD）患者の活動期において細菌のasRNA発現パターンが収束し、便中カルプロテクチンなどの炎症指標と相関することが示された。asRNAの動態は挿入配列エレメントにおけるアンチセンスからセンスへの転写シフトを引き起こし、ゲノム構造の再編に先立って適応機能を提示していた。同様の現象はマウスの大腸炎モデルや病原体感染性胃腸炎患者でも確認され、asRNAが病態適応の重要な要素であることが明らかになった。
summary_en: Researchers established metastrand, an analytical platform integrating strand-aware metatranscriptomics and metagenomics to quantify bacterial mRNA and antisense RNA dynamics. In inflammatory bowel disease, gut microbial antisense RNA profiles converged during active disease and correlated with fecal inflammatory markers. These antisense RNA shifts preceded genomic rearrangements, demonstrating that antisense transcription serves as a key mechanism for microbial adaptation during inflammation.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌のアンチセンスRNA転写動態は、炎症性腸疾患などの病態におけるゲノム再編と環境適応を駆動する。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌の病態適応メカニズムの理解を深め、炎症性腸疾患の新たな診断バイオマーカーや治療標的の開発につながる可能性がある。
